title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Servicing of Loans in Default and VA Partial Claims
content:
This part of the servicing standards of the VA Home Loan Guaranty governs loans in default.

### Default

A loan is reported in default when a payment is past due by the program's default-reporting number of days.

### Home retention before liquidation

The servicer must consider home retention before liquidation, in this order: repayment plan, forbearance, loan modification, then a VA partial claim, then a compromise sale or deed in lieu. A servicer may not make the first foreclosure filing before the program's minimum number of days of delinquency.

### The VA partial claim

- A partial claim is paid only on a loan whose status is in default; the loan record is the authority, read before the partial claim is booked.
- It requires at least the program's minimum number of missed monthly payments.
- The clause that a partial claim never exceeds the program's partial claim ceiling percentage of the unpaid principal balance at the first unpaid installment is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for figuring the partial claim paid.
- It bears the program's partial claim interest rate.
- It becomes due when the loan is paid off, refinanced or the home sold.

### Decisions that belong to the servicer

The servicer, not VA, decides plans, forbearance and modifications. VA's agent can explain those options but cannot approve them.

## Status test (hypothetical loans)

| Loan record status | Partial claim may be paid |
|---|---|
| In default | Yes, subject to the other conditions above |
| Active (current) | No |
| Paid in full, foreclosed or released by assumption | No |

## Basis questions

**Can VA's agent grant a forbearance?** No. The servicer decides forbearance; the agent can explain it.

**When is the partial claim repaid?** When the loan is paid off, refinanced or the home sold.
